_what_this_is: The text calibration re-read through a local llama.cpp HTTP server, case by case against the recorded one-shot CLI reading, to show the two transports read the same quantity.
_why_this_file_exists: The runtime reaches the watch model over a server (`src/llama.ts`), because the resident context of `agent-lifecycle.md` §4 lives in the model's own KV cache and a process per judgement throws that cache away with the process. But the shipped 0.600 cut was measured through a one-shot CLI scorer, so an adapter on a different transport had to be shown to read the same estimator before it could be allowed to keep that cut. A reading taken the other way -- one masked id per option -- would not be a second implementation of this cut, it would be a second cut.

shape.prompt: the artifact's system line as a chat system message, then the assembled remainder as a user turn, rendered by the server's own chat template (/apply-template) -- the shape calibration/vision/remeasured.json was taken in
shape.answer_read: the next-token distribution at the prompt's own end (/completion, n_predict 1, n_probs 64), summed over every candidate whose decoded form strips to the option (lowercase, letters and digits only) -- the estimator calibration/provenance.md describes for the text run
shape.samplers: neutral (temperature 1, top_k 0, top_p 1, min_p 0, repeat_penalty 1), so the reading is the raw softmax and not a sampled or truncated one
shape.note: the mask ids are measured on the TEMPLATED text, because the answer is read after the template's own tail; src/llama.ts bindOverServer does this by tokenising the templated prompt and the templated prompt plus each option

latency.note: the CLI figure is a fresh process per case; the server figure is a warm one, which is the point of the transport

what_this_settles: A server-based reader reproduces the calibrated probability to within 0.0008 on all 24 cases, so the adapter built on it keeps the 0.600 cut in src/prompts/watch-v1.json rather than needing its own.
The 20/24 at the shipped cut is the same 20/24 the CLI rig recorded -- including act 8/12 -- so the gap at 0.600 is the operating point and not the transport.
Reading each case costs 114 ms warm against 186 ms cold, so the resident context is doing what §4 says it is for.
what_this_does_not_settle: Nothing about which model ships: line 25 of src/README.md is still open, and the multilingual half is still measured and unmet (act 1/6 on the twelve Chinese cases).

Nothing about images in this file. This run is the text set only -- /completion takes no projector, so the image sets could not travel this way. They have since been replayed through the endpoint that does take one, case by case against the same recorded reading, and every image figure is in server-transport-images.json; none is quoted here.

Nothing about the cut itself. 0.600 is what the artifact declares and what governs; the re-measurement that says one cut near 0.39 serves both paths is calibration/vision/remeasured.json's, and moving the number is the design's to do.

The estimator is summed over the top 64 candidates, not over the whole vocabulary. At this depth the omitted mass is far below any cut in the measured plateaus, but it is not zero and a shallower n_probs would under-report.
